common_name: Gran's Favourite Dianthus (White Laced Reddish-Purple Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Gran's Favourite bears white semi-double flowers heavily laced in reddish-purple, holder of an RHS Award of Garden Merit.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Gran's Favourite, a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit garden pink, bears semi-double white flowers intricately laced with a fine reddish-purple pattern radiating from the center, a refined old-fashioned look prized by dianthus collectors, carried on a compact, fragrant, blue-green foliage mound. It shows good heat tolerance for the class when grown in sharply drained, lean soil. Shear lightly after the main spring bloom to keep the foliage mat dense and tidy through the rest of the season.

common_name: Haytor White Dianthus (Pure White Fragrant Double Garden Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Haytor White bears pure white, fragrant, showy double flowers on a compact garden pink, holder of an RHS Award of Garden Merit.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Haytor White, a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit garden pink, bears clean, pure white, fully double flowers with the strong, spicy clove fragrance typical of the best garden pinks, popular both as a garden plant and as a cut flower for its long vase life. Its compact, blue-green foliage mound is neat and evergreen year-round. Shear lightly after the main spring bloom to keep the foliage mat dense and tidy through the rest of the season.

common_name: Pike's Pink Dianthus (Double Orchid-Pink Opening from Creamy Buds)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Pike's Pink bears double orchid-pink flowers opening from creamy-yellow buds on a low, wide blue-green mound.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Pike's Pink bears double, fragrant, orchid-pink flowers that emerge from distinctive creamy-yellow buds, opening over a low, wide-spreading mound of fine blue-green foliage that makes an excellent edging or rock garden plant. Its dense, cushion-like habit and reliable spring bloom have kept it a long-standing favorite for sunny, well-drained borders. Shear lightly after the main spring bloom to keep the foliage mat dense and tidy through the rest of the season.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Inchmery is an old 18th-century double pale shell-pink garden pink with strong clove fragrance.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Inchmery, dating to the eighteenth century, is one of the oldest named garden pinks still in cultivation, bearing soft, pale shell-pink, double flowers with an intense, spicy clove fragrance considered by many collectors among the finest of any dianthus. Its long history and reliable performance have kept it a treasured heirloom for cottage-garden and historic plantings. Shear lightly after the main spring bloom to keep the foliage mat dense and tidy through the rest of the season.

common_name: Constance Finnis Dianthus (Historic Pale-Pink Spicy-Scented Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Constance Finnis, grown since roughly 1700, bears pale-pink, mildly spicy-scented semi-double flowers.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Constance Finnis, grown continuously since roughly 1700, bears soft pale-pink, semi-double flowers with a mild, pleasant spicy scent, a historic garden pink whose long cultivation history makes it a favorite for heritage and cottage-garden plantings. Its compact, fragrant, evergreen blue-green foliage provides year-round structure at the front of a border. Shear lightly after the main spring bloom to keep the foliage mat dense and tidy through the rest of the season.

common_name: La Bourboule Dianthus (Compact Alpine Pink with Toothed Petals)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; La Bourboule is a compact, mat-forming alpine pink with small single, bright rose-pink, toothed-petal flowers.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. La Bourboule forms a dense, tight, mat-forming cushion of fine blue-green foliage rarely more than a few inches tall, topped in spring with abundant small, single, bright rose-pink flowers with delicately toothed petal edges, an alpine-scale garden pink well suited to rock gardens, troughs, and tight crevices between paving stones. Its low, spreading habit makes it one of the most useful dianthus selections for a small-scale rock garden setting. Shear lightly after the main spring bloom to keep the foliage mat dense and tidy through the rest of the season.

common_name: Rose de Mai Dianthus (Earliest-Blooming Intensely Clove-Scented Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Rose de Mai is the earliest-blooming garden pink, often flowering in March, with clear-pink, double, intensely clove-scented flowers.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Rose de Mai is prized as the earliest-blooming garden pink cultivar, often opening its clear-pink, double, intensely clove-scented flowers as early as March, well ahead of most other dianthus selections, extending the fragrant-pink season at the start of spring. Its compact, evergreen, blue-green foliage mound provides tidy structure at the front of a border year-round. Shear lightly after the main spring bloom to keep the foliage mat dense and tidy through the rest of the season.

common_name: Coconut Sundae Dianthus (White with Red-Pink Center, Repeat-Blooming)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Coconut Sundae, part of the Scent First series, bears white petals with a vivid red-pink center on a repeat-blooming fragrant double pink.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Coconut Sundae, part of the Scent First breeding series, bears double flowers in crisp white with a vivid red-pink eye at the center, a bold bicolor combination on a fragrant, repeat-blooming plant bred to flower over a longer season than many older dianthus cultivars. Its extended bloom period and strong clove scent make it a strong performer for a sunny border or container. Shear lightly after the main spring bloom to keep the foliage mat dense and encourage continued rebloom.

common_name: Dad's Favourite Dianthus (Historic White Laced in Velvety Maroon)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Dad's Favourite is a historic Paisley/laced pink from the 1800s with white semi-double flowers laced in velvety maroon.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Dad's Favourite, a historic Paisley or laced garden pink dating to the 1800s, bears white, semi-double flowers intricately laced with velvety maroon, an elegant patterned bloom typical of the antique laced pink class prized by heritage garden collectors. Its long cultivation history and refined form have kept it a favorite among dianthus enthusiasts. Shear lightly after the main spring bloom to keep the foliage mat dense and tidy through the rest of the season.

common_name: Waithman Beauty Dianthus (Ruby-Red Marked with Pink-White Lacing)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Waithman Beauty bears ruby-red to dark magenta-maroon flowers marked with pale pink-white lacing, sweetly clove-scented.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Waithman Beauty bears deep ruby-red to dark magenta-maroon flowers finely marked with pale pink-white lacing, a rich, dramatic laced pattern on a strongly clove-scented old-style garden pink, opening over compact, evergreen blue-green foliage. Its dark, jewel-toned color makes a bold accent at the front of a sunny border. Shear lightly after the main spring bloom to keep the foliage mat dense and tidy through the rest of the season.

common_name: Brympton Red Dianthus (Heritage Deep Red Garden Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Brympton Red is an RHS-listed heritage garden pink with deep red flowers.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Brympton Red, a Royal Horticultural Society-listed heritage garden pink, bears deep, solid red flowers with the strong clove fragrance typical of the best garden pinks, opening over compact, evergreen blue-green foliage. Its rich, saturated color and heirloom pedigree make it a strong choice for a historic or cottage-garden border. Shear lightly after the main spring bloom to keep the foliage mat dense and tidy through the rest of the season.
